title: FLUX profile document, format 1-4-0
description: Aggregate statistics of the data a FLUX bundle imitates, computed where the data lives. Counts are JSON integers and every other number is a decimal string. The shape is checked here; docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md states the rules a schema cannot express (registered definitions, sorted groups and levels, cells that line up with their statuses, names that refer to columns and tables of the profile). Format 1-2-0 adds the invariants section and, for a profiler that releases aggregates under differential privacy, the privacy block, a noise block on a count statistic and noisy cliques, and changes nothing format 1-1-0 says: this schema validates documents of formats 1-0-0 to 1-2-0 too, and the reader refuses a document that names 1-0-0 and holds a quantile/2 statistic, or names 1-0-0 or 1-1-0 and holds an invariants section, a privacy block, a noise block or cliques. Format 1-3-0 adds the references section, a groupBy on a number column, groupByLink and per, a table's datePairs and calendar and a relationship's dates and exposure, and a groupBy on the one statistic a query holds (a query's rate per group), all optional; the reader refuses a document that names an earlier format and holds one. Format 1-4-0 adds the rank correlations kendallTau/1 and spearmanRho/1 in a columnPairs entry, exact or released with noise, and the rowFloor key of such a statistic, all optional; the reader refuses a document that names an earlier format and holds one. It also adds the clique cliqueMarginal/2, which holds one to 32 category, number or timestamp columns with bins for the last two, a table's cliqueSelection, which says how its cliques were chosen and what that spent (a measured selection only), and a groupByBins on a column statistic, all optional; the reader refuses a document that names an earlier format and holds one.

_producer.description: The tool that wrote the profile (OpenLineage BaseFacet).

_schemaURL.description: The $id of the format the document is written in (OpenLineage BaseFacet): this schema's own, or format 1-0-0's or 1-1-0's. A document that holds a quantile/2 statistic names 1-1-0 or 1-2-0, and one that holds an invariants section names 1-2-0. A document that holds a kendallTau/1 or spearmanRho/1 statistic or a rowFloor names 1-4-0.

Count.description: A count: a JSON integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1.

Decimal.description: An exact decimal written as a string: no exponent, no plus sign, no leading zeros, and at most 1000 digits.

Units.description: An integer on the grid, written as a string with at most 1000 digits, as S writes an encoded sum.

Name.description: A non-empty name, in Unicode Normalization Form C.

GroupKey.description: A group key: the empty string for an ungrouped statistic.

Status.description: An SDMX CL_CONF_STATUS 1.4 code; F is published.

SuppressedStatus.description: A CL_CONF_STATUS code other than F.

SampleSize.description: The band the number of records behind a statistic lies in.

DisclosureRule.description: A disclosure rule in ACRO's terms; an absent field was not applied.

QuantileBinGroup.description: A published quantile/2 group: the bin of the statistic's bins that holds the order statistic, and the records below and through that bin. It states no witness.

quantileBin.description: The index of the bin that holds the order statistic; null exactly when k is 0, as quantile/1's witness is.

groupBy.description: Format 1-4-0. A category column of the relationship's parent table: the parents are grouped by its value.

groupByBins.description: Format 1-4-0. A number or timestamp column of the relationship's parent table, grouped by these bins.

noise.description: Format 1-4-0, on a marginalHistogram/1 only (PROFILE-SPEC.md section 3a).

Metrics.description: OpenLineage's columnMetrics names, as integer counts and decimal strings.

TimestampMetricValues.description: A timestamp column's min, max and quantile values: integer milliseconds since the epoch.

datePairs.description: Statistics of the days between two timestamp columns of the table (format 1-3-0).

calendar.description: The known values of a timestamp column by month, day of week and hour of week, read in UTC (format 1-3-0).

structural.description: Classes of parents the source's own constraints leave empty: childless (every parent has a child) and orphan (every non-NULL child key has its parent).

dates.description: Statistics of the days between a parent's timestamp column and a child's (format 1-3-0).

exposure.description: The exposure of a parent's lifetime columns to children inside a window (format 1-3-0).

start.description: Integer milliseconds since the epoch, in decimal text.

end.description: Integer milliseconds since the epoch, in decimal text.

PrivacyLoss.description: A privacy loss: rho under zero-concentrated DP, or epsilon and delta under approximate DP. The measure of the privacy block says which, and the reader checks that every part is in that measure.

Privacy.description: The release-level account of a profile released under differential privacy (PROFILE-SPEC.md section 3a): the measure, the total privacy loss and the unit of privacy. Names are OpenDP's, as a vocabulary only.

expose.description: One row of this expose is the unit: neighbouring data sets differ by adding or removing one row of it, together with the rows that follow it when the unit lists relationships in follows.

follows.description: Format 1-4-0. The relationships whose child rows go with a row of the expose. Each names one entry of the profile's relationships and a fixed public cap on children per parent row. The entries form a tree rooted at the expose: a table is the child of one entry only, the parent of every entry is the expose or the child of another, and there is no cycle (PROFILE-SPEC.md section 3a).

publicStructure.description: True when the levels and bin edges of the profile's histograms and cliques, the bins of every groupByBins, the group keys of its grouped noisy statistics, the sampleSize bands, every rowFloor and every maxChildren were chosen without the data, or are part of the release. The engine cannot check it, and a profile without it is not graded P3.

Noise.description: The mechanism, scale and share of the budget that a noisy statistic or clique was released under.

NoisyGroup.description: A group of a noisy count statistic: one noisy value per cell, each a decimal string that can be negative or fractional.

Clique.description: A noisy clique marginal (PROFILE-SPEC.md section 5a): the joint count table of two or more categorical columns of one table, one noisy value per combination of levels, row-major with the first column slowest.

ReferenceTable.description: The rows of a table released whole (format 1-3-0): every row has one cell per column, and a cell is a string or null.

LinkGroup.description: A grouping by a column of the row a relationship names (format 1-3-0).

DatePairStatistic.description: A statistic of the days from a date pair's start to its end (format 1-3-0): a histogram or a quantile, optionally grouped by a column of the table, optionally noisy.

DatePairOrder.description: The order of a date pair's end against its start (format 1-3-0): a level histogram over the three levels.

RelationshipDateStatistic.description: A statistic of the days from a parent's date to a child's across a relationship (format 1-3-0).

RelationshipDateOrder.description: The order of a child's date against its parent's across a relationship (format 1-3-0).

CalendarMonth.description: The month histogram of a calendar entry (format 1-3-0): a level histogram over exactly the levels the format fixes, optionally noisy.

CalendarDayOfWeek.description: The dayOfWeek histogram of a calendar entry (format 1-3-0): a level histogram over exactly the levels the format fixes, optionally noisy.

CalendarHourOfWeek.description: The hourOfWeek histogram of a calendar entry (format 1-3-0): a level histogram over exactly the levels the format fixes, optionally noisy.

CountMetric.description: A count/1 metric: an exact count, or a withheld one that holds no value.

GroupedQueryStatistic.description: A query's rate, which format 1-3-0 lets be grouped by a column of the query's rows. A fact's share (Invariant) is never grouped.

History.description: The versions of one table's entities: its validity window, how many versions an entity has, when it starts, how long a version lasts, how consecutive versions meet, how the last one ends, and for each candidate tracked column its first value, its transitions and the changes that move it.

RankFloor.description: The row floor of a rank correlation: a count of at least 2, chosen without the data. The statistic is formed over N = max(n, rowFloor) records, where n is the number of records behind it.

group.description: A rank correlation is ungrouped: its one group is keyed by the empty string.

S.description: The sum over every pair of records of sign(a_i - a_j) * sign(b_i - b_j), a tied pair adding 0.

group.description: A rank correlation is ungrouped: its one group is keyed by the empty string.

A4.description: Four times the sum of the products of the centred mid-ranks of the two columns.

NoisyRankGroup.description: The group of a noisy rank correlation: the released value, a decimal string that may lie outside [-1, 1], and no S, A4 or k.

KendallTau.description: kendallTau/1, a rank correlation of a column pair (format 1-4-0). Noise needs a rowFloor.

SpearmanRho.description: spearmanRho/1, a rank correlation of a column pair (format 1-4-0). Noise needs a rowFloor.

Clique2.description: A noisy clique marginal over one to 32 columns, each a category, a number or a timestamp (format 1-4-0, PROFILE-SPEC.md section 5a). A category column lists its levels, a number or timestamp column its bin edges. One noisy value per combination of levels and bins, row-major with the first column slowest. The reader refuses a clique with an estimate: this format reads measured cliques only.

CliqueDomain.description: The levels of a category column of a clique, or the bin edges of a number or timestamp column (format 1-4-0).

BinEdges.description: Bin edges, at least two, strictly increasing decimals (format 1-4-0).

BinGrouping.description: A grouping by the bin of another number or timestamp column of the table (format 1-4-0). The groups are keyed by the canonical decimal text of each bin's lower edge, and the records whose value is NULL are one more group, never written.

CliqueSelection.description: How a table's cliques were chosen and released (format 1-4-0): the method, the tool that chose and measured them, the share spent choosing them (absent for a method that named them before the data was read) and the share spent releasing levels or bin edges that were not public. Both shares are parts of the account, in its measure. Only measured cliques are read.

selection.description: The share spent choosing the cliques.

domain.description: The share spent releasing levels or bin edges that were not public.
